ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are two 4×4 grids on the left and right. Record coordinates by taking the rows from top to bottom as rows 1 to 4, and the columns from left to right as columns 1 to 4. The shaded cells in the left figure are (1,3),(1,4),(2,3),(2,4),(3,1),(3,2),(3,3),(4,2). The shaded cells in the right figure are (1,1),(1,3),(2,2),(2,4),(3,1),(3,3),(4,2),(4,4). Reasoning: Comparing the left and right figures, the cells that are already shaded in common are (1,3),(2,4),(3,1),(3,3),(4,2). The extra shaded cells in the left figure are S={(1,4),(2,3),(3,2)}, and the shaded cells that need to be added in the right figure are D={(1,1),(2,2),(4,4)}. One move can only exchange two cells in the same row or the same column, so if a shaded cell is to go to a target cell in the same row or the same column, at least 1 step is needed; if both the row and the column are different, then it must pass through an intermediate crossing position, and at least 2 steps are needed. From this, the costs from S to D are obtained: from (1,4) to (1,1),(2,2),(4,4) are respectively 1,2,1; from (2,3) to them are respectively 2,1,2; from (3,2) to them are respectively 2,1,2. The minimum matching cost is 4, therefore at least 4 steps are needed. Construct 4 steps: exchange (1,4) and (1,1); exchange (2,3) and (2,2); exchange (3,2) and (3,4); exchange (3,4) and (4,4). After these four exchanges, the shaded cells exactly become as shown in the right figure. Therefore the minimum number of steps is 4.
